Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

Fitted candidates (all on the same data, 126 readings):

Candidate C9 (asprey_2000_monod_kinetics eq 17, rate law r = theta1*x2/(theta2 + x2)):
asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + asprey_2000_monod_kinetics eq 17: chi2 241.2 vs limit 148.8 (LACK OF FIT); AIC 249.2; probability 0.000
   theta1   0.2848  95% CI [0.2778, 0.2918]  t 40.87
   theta2   0.06385  95% CI [0.05971, 0.06799]  t 15.42
   theta3   0.4858  95% CI [0.4723, 0.4994]  t 35.77
   theta4   0.03547  95% CI [0.03028, 0.04066]  t 6.83
   misfit mostly in: E2:x2 (chi2 80 over 21 readings, model over-predicts on average, worst at t=5 h); E1:x2 (chi2 58 over 21 readings, model under-predicts on average, worst at t=2 h); E3:x2 (chi2 36 over 21 readings, model under-predicts on average, worst at t=19 h)

Candidate C8 (asprey_2000_contois_kinetics eq 18, rate law r = theta1*x2/(theta2*x1 + x2)):
asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + asprey_2000_contois_kinetics eq 18: chi2 106.5 vs limit 148.8 (fits within the noise); AIC 114.5; probability 1.000
   theta1   0.3024  95% CI [0.2943, 0.3106]  t 37.25
   theta2   0.0109  95% CI [0.01023, 0.01158]  t 16.23

asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + muloiwa_2020_free_laws eq 6: chi2 240.4 vs limit 147.7 (LACK OF FIT); AIC 250.4; probability 0.000
   Ki       235.7  95% CI [-259.4, 730.8]  t 0.48  <- not estimated precisely

Round 1 of 3. Decide. If you accept, 'chosen' is the candidate label, e.g. C9.

answer.feedback: C8 fits the data, and its improvement over C9/C27 suggests growth kinetics need a biomass-dependent effect. However, C8's theta1 is strongly correlated with both theta3 and theta4, so those parameters are not separable and it does not meet the requirement that every parameter be estimated precisely. Seek a more identifiable, preferably parsimonious formulation or experiments that separate these effects. The biomass-independent C9/C27 models overpredict E2 substrate x2 (worst at 5 h) and underpredict E1 x2 (2 h) and E3 x2 (19 h); use the differing experiment conditions to refine the biomass dependence.
answer.reasoning: C9 and C27 fail the chi-square limit. C27 also has an imprecise Ki. C8 is the only candidate that fits within the noise and all its reported t-values exceed 1, but its strong parameter correlations mean key parameters are not separable from these data. Thus no candidate currently satisfies all acceptance criteria.
